controls.title: Infrastructure at rest uses the AWS service-default key
controls.statement: Infrastructure at rest (Terraform state, DynamoDB, S3, SQS, CloudWatch Logs and Secrets Manager) is encrypted with the AWS service-default key, AWS-owned or aws/<service> managed. A customer-managed key on infrastructure fails unless its resource carries a rationale comment naming cross-account access or a service-principal publisher that needs one, because each such key adds a monthly charge and a key policy to keep right.
controls.look_for: An aws_kms_key, kms_key_id, kms_master_key_id or kms_key_arn on an infrastructure resource with no rationale comment beside it; sse_algorithm aws:kms with a customer key on a bucket that holds no product key material.

controls.title: Product keys are customer-managed, multi-Region and rotated
controls.statement: A product key (key material the product creates or manages for its customers) is a customer-managed key with multi_region = true, enable_key_rotation = true and an explicit key policy. A product key on an AWS-managed key, without rotation, without a key policy, or shared with an infrastructure resource fails, because the two key classes then share one blast radius and one access policy.
controls.look_for: A product key resource missing multi_region, enable_key_rotation or a key policy; one aws_kms_key referenced by both a product resource and an infrastructure resource.

controls.title: Buckets use SSE-S3 with the bucket key left on
controls.statement: Buckets are encrypted with SSE-S3 (sse_algorithm AES256) unless the COST-KMS-1 exception applies. A bucket on a customer-managed key without that rationale comment fails, and bucket_key_enabled = false fails, because each turns every object request into a billed KMS call.
controls.look_for: sse_algorithm aws:kms with no COST-KMS-1 rationale comment; bucket_key_enabled = false; BucketKeyEnabled false.

controls.title: Compute runs on arm64 and paid capacity carries a rationale
controls.statement: Lambda functions and container tasks choose arm64 where the runtime allows. An x86_64 architecture without a stated runtime reason fails, and provisioned concurrency or reserved capacity without a rationale comment fails, because each costs more for the same work and reserved capacity bills while idle.
controls.look_for: architectures x86_64 or no architectures on a Lambda; cpu_architecture X86_64 on a task definition; provisioned_concurrent_executions or reserved capacity with no rationale comment.

controls.title: DynamoDB tables are on-demand by default
controls.statement: DynamoDB tables use on-demand capacity (billing_mode PAY_PER_REQUEST). A provisioned table without a rationale comment, or without autoscaling on its read and write capacity, fails, because fixed capacity bills while idle and throttles past its limit.
controls.look_for: billing_mode PROVISIONED or absent with read_capacity and write_capacity set; a provisioned table with no aws_appautoscaling_target or no rationale comment.

controls.title: No NAT gateway, interface endpoint or load balancer without a rationale
controls.statement: A NAT gateway, an interface VPC endpoint or a load balancer carries a rationale comment, and S3 and DynamoDB are reached through gateway endpoints. One without the comment fails, because each bills by the hour whether or not traffic flows, and a NAT gateway also bills per gigabyte for traffic a free gateway endpoint carries.
controls.look_for: aws_nat_gateway, vpc_endpoint_type Interface, aws_lb, aws_alb or aws_elb with no rationale comment; S3 or DynamoDB traffic routed through a NAT gateway with no gateway endpoint.

controls.title: Every log group sets a retention
controls.statement: Every CloudWatch log group sets retention_in_days to a value above 0. A log group with no retention, or with 0 (never expire), fails, because its storage then grows and bills without end.
controls.look_for: aws_cloudwatch_log_group without retention_in_days; retention_in_days = 0; a Lambda or service that creates its own log group with no managed log group beside it.

controls.title: Terraform state is in S3 with S3 native locking
controls.statement: The state backend is S3 with use_lockfile = true and no DynamoDB lock table. A backend with a dynamodb_table, or without use_lockfile, fails, because the lock table is a second resource to pay for and keep, and without either lock two applies can corrupt the state.
controls.look_for: backend s3 without use_lockfile = true; dynamodb_table in a backend block; a local or other backend for shared state.
